title: Cross-survey style mixing inside the borrowed eyes: during training, the early trunk layers' per-channel feature statistics (the 'look' of a photograph) are randomly blended with another view's from a different survey, so the place description cannot key on any one survey's style
hypothesis: Builds on experiments 12-13 (pretrained trunk, kept) and experiment 4 (pixel-level nuisance randomisation, kept), and is the feature-level successor to experiment 6 (pixel blending of surveys, reverted). Experiments 12->13 moved held-out truedop_2024 usable from 10.75% to 49.5% to 60.25% (false fix 7.0 -> 5.5 -> 3.75%) purely by giving the place feature more of the ImageNet trunk's invariance: the stage that decides what a place looks like is where transfer to a new survey is won. But the trunk still encodes survey: exp 13's clean survey diagnostic on TRAINING positions ends at xs_cos_same 0.657, within-place variance fraction 0.235 and cross-survey argmax agreement only ~0.74 between the three training photographs, while the training photographs themselves score 0.013-0.038 (97-99% usable) and the held-out one 0.435 with 36% abstention. So a quarter of the embedding's variance is still 'which survey', and on a fourth survey that shifts the embedding off its tile prototype, which the committee min-mass gate turns into an abstention (coverage 64%, but 94% of answered frames correct). The answer is not more decode gating; it is a trunk whose mid-level features carry less survey style. Pixel-level augmentation (exp 4) can only perturb global exposure/colour/blur; the survey differences that remain (season, canopy, shadow length, texture rendering, sharpening/compression of each orthophoto pipeline) live in the per-channel mean and std of early CNN feature maps, which is exactly what style-transfer work identifies as 'style' (AdaIN). MixStyle (Zhou et al., ICLR 2021) regularises a pretrained CNN against unseen domains by replacing, at random during training, each instance's early-layer channel statistics with a convex mix of its own and another instance's. Our batches are survey-mixed by construction (paired-position interleave), so the partner is a different survey's photograph about two-thirds of the time: every place is shown wearing styles interpolated between the three surveys, which is the continuum experiment 6 tried to create in pixel space but with the content (spatial layout of the feature map) left intact rather than ghosted. A fourth survey's style is far more likely to fall inside that continuum than on one of three points.
method: Training-only change in model/model.py: add a parameter-free MixStyle module and apply it inside Member.embed() after MobileNetV3-Small trunk blocks features[1], features[3] and features[6] (outputs 16x32x32, 24x16x16, 40x8x8 at 128 px input: the early/mid levels where channel statistics encode style, not the deep 96x4x4 level that carries layout). In training mode with probability p=0.5 per batch per insertion point: per-instance per-channel mean mu and std sig over H,W (sig = sqrt(var+1e-6), both detached), normalise x_hat=(x-mu)/sig, draw lambda ~ Beta(0.1,0.1) per instance, pick partner by a random permutation of the batch, mix mu_mix = lambda*mu + (1-lambda)*mu[perm], sig_mix likewise, output x_hat*sig_mix + mu_mix. In eval mode (and therefore in the ONNX export and the survey diagnostic) it is the identity, so the deployed graph is unchanged. Each committee member draws its own MixStyle randomness (they already get independent augment_views draws). Nothing else changes: same trunk, lifts, cosine head, committee decode, losses, augmentation, LR groups, epochs.
expected_outcome: truedop_2024 mission 0.435 -> ~0.33-0.38: usable 60.25% -> 65-70% (abstentions converting to confident correct fixes as each place's embedding moves less with survey), false fix held at <=4% (the committee gate is unchanged). Training-capture diagnostics stay within ~0.02 of today (0.013-0.038), possibly slightly worse, since the model loses some survey-specific shortcuts. Logged survey diagnostic should show wpv falling below 0.235 and xsurvey_agree rising above ~0.74. Refutation: if wpv falls but 2024 usable does not rise, early-layer style was not what separates 2024 from the training surveys and the remaining gap is content (season/canopy/construction), pointing next at the deep layers or at the training targets rather than at style. If usable falls, the mixing removed signal the pretrained invariances were already handling.
init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR (unchanged from experiment 13)
eli5: Each of the three aerial surveys of Berlin has its own 'look': one is a lush summer, one bare winter trees, one early spring, each processed by a different camera and lab. The model's early layers notice that look as overall averages, a bit like a photo filter. While training, we now randomly swap a blend of another survey's filter onto each picture inside the model, keeping the streets and rooftops exactly where they are. The model sees every street in many in-between styles, so a fourth survey with a style it has never seen looks like more of the same, and it has to recognise the place itself.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent copies of the first eleven blocks of MobileNetV3-Small, pre-trained on ImageNet (open BSD-3 licence) and fine-tuned on Berlin at a tenth of the usual learning rate. Each reads the frame at two depths: a 48-channel 8×8 map (edges and textures) and a deeper 96-channel 4×4 map (how roads, roofs and trees are arranged across the frame). Each depth is lifted to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame; the two halves together are the 112-number description of the place. Identical in flight to experiment 13

stages.name: Map-cell classifier
stages.detail: each extractor's description is centred, scaled to unit length and compared by angle against one unit-length reference direction per map tile (~3,000 tiles, 128 m each) - a compass, not a lookup table; the angle match times a fixed sharpness (30) is the tile score. The two members' tile-belief maps are averaged to pick the tile

stages.name: Local belief pooling
stages.detail: gathers the averaged belief spread over the winning tile AND its 8 neighbours, and places the fix at the balance point of that local cluster instead of snapping to one tile's centre

stages.name: Within-cell offset
stages.detail: small head per member that nudges the fix from the pooled balance point to the exact spot; the two nudges are averaged

stages.name: Confidence gate
stages.detail: confidence = the SMALLER of the two members' belief on the winning tile plus its 8 neighbours — both navigators must independently back the same place; if either one spreads its belief elsewhere the drone abstains

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: NEW: cross-survey style mixing. Inside the feature extractor, after its 2nd, 4th and 7th blocks, half the time each training view's per-channel feature averages and spreads (its photographic 'style') are blended with those of another view in the batch, usually from a different survey, while the spatial layout is untouched; switched off in flight. Everything else as experiment 13: angular-margin tile loss, offset loss, paired three-survey batches, re-photographing augmentation, pre-trained blocks at a tenth of the learning rate, targets, epochs and views per epoch unchanged

implementation_brief:
ONE change, training-only: MixStyle feature-statistic mixing inside each member's pretrained trunk. Files: model/model.py (main change), model/train.py (logging/metadata only).

model/model.py:
1. Add constants near the other module constants: MIXSTYLE_AFTER = (1, 3, 6)  # indices into trunk (features[i]) after which MixStyle runs; MIXSTYLE_P = 0.5; MIXSTYLE_ALPHA = 0.1; MIXSTYLE_EPS = 1e-6.
2. Add a parameter-free class MixStyle(nn.Module) with __init__(self, p=MIXSTYLE_P, alpha=MIXSTYLE_ALPHA, eps=MIXSTYLE_EPS) storing p/alpha/eps and creating self.beta = torch.distributions.Beta(alpha, alpha) lazily or sampling via torch.distributions.Beta(torch.tensor(alpha), torch.tensor(alpha)).sample((B,1,1,1)).to(x.device, x.dtype) (sample on CPU then move; MPS lacks some Beta kernels). forward(x): `if not self.training or x.shape[0] < 2 or torch.rand(1).item() > self.p: return x` — this Python-level check runs once per batch per insertion point, NOT per-sample and is acceptable (it is a CPU RNG, no device sync). Otherwise: B = x.shape[0]; mu = x.mean(dim=(2,3), keepdim=True); var = x.var(dim=(2,3), keepdim=True); sig = (var + eps).sqrt(); mu, sig = mu.detach(), sig.detach(); x_norm = (x - mu) / sig; lmda = Beta sample [B,1,1,1]; perm = torch.randperm(B, device=x.device); mu_mix = mu*lmda + mu[perm]*(1-lmda); sig_mix = sig*lmda + sig[perm]*(1-lmda); return x_norm*sig_mix + mu_mix. No parameters, no buffers (so state_dict keys and ONNX are unchanged).
3. In Member.__init__ add self.mixstyle = MixStyle() (one module instance is fine; it is stateless). Do NOT put it inside self.trunk (trunk_parameters()/head_parameters() split and strict pretrained load must be untouched; it has no parameters anyway).
4. Rewrite Member.embed() to run the 11 trunk blocks one by one: `h = xn; for i, blk in enumerate(self.trunk): h = blk(h); if i in MIXSTYLE_AFTER: h = self.mixstyle(h); if i == TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS - 1: h_mid = h` and after the loop h_deep = h. Then the existing lift_mid/lift_deep/GAP/concat/embed_bn/normalize lines unchanged, returning (e, f). In eval mode this must be numerically identical to the current slice-based embed (MixStyle is identity). Note MIXSTYLE_AFTER indices are all < TRUNK_MID_BLOCKS-1 = 8, so h_mid is taken after block 8 as today.
5. Add a short 'CROSS-SURVEY STYLE MIXING (capture-holdout era, experiment 14)' paragraph to the module docstring: what MixStyle does, insertion points features[1]/[3]/[6] (16x32x32, 24x16x16, 40x8x8), p=0.5, Beta(0.1,0.1), partner = random permutation of the survey-mixed batch, identity in eval/export.
6. Leave untouched: CELL_PX, N_MEMBERS, EMBED_DIM, LIFT_DIM, trunk construction and strict load from mnv3s_features10.pt, ImageNet normalisation buffers, cosine head, COS_SCALE/COS_MARGIN, CellLocNet (forward decode, block_mask, training_outputs), loss_fn, export_onnx, estimate_position.

model/train.py:
7. Import MIXSTYLE_AFTER, MIXSTYLE_P, MIXSTYLE_ALPHA from model.model; add them to the startup print line and to the returned info dict as "mixstyle": {"after_blocks": list(MIXSTYLE_AFTER), "p": MIXSTYLE_P, "alpha": MIXSTYLE_ALPHA}; append ', MixStyle cross-survey feature-statistic mixing after trunk blocks 1/3/6 (train only)' to the capture_sampling string; add one sentence to the module docstring. No change to the training loop, augmentation, optimiser groups, scheduler, survey_diag (which runs model.eval(), so it measures the deployed, mixing-free embedding — keep it that way), or export. Make sure survey_diag and export run in eval mode (they already do: survey_diag calls model.eval(); export_onnx calls model.eval()).

Contracts to preserve (the frozen scorer depends on them): train.py CLI unchanged — `python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--data-dir D] [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket M] [--seed S]`, writes <out>/models/<area>.onnx and appends to <out>/train_info.json. ONNX: input 'frame' 1x3x128x128 float32 in [0,1], output 'uvc' [[u, v, conf]] with u,v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1], opset 17, dynamo=False; the exported graph must contain no MixStyle ops (export in eval mode). Training reads only buckets(meta, "train"); nothing under model/ may open the eval capture truedop_2024 in any form. Keep per-step code free of device->host syncs other than the single torch.rand(1).item() CPU draw (that is a CPU tensor, no sync). Size/latency gates: unchanged model, ~7.45 MB fp32, well within 32 MiB / 250 ms. Sanity check before exiting: build the model, run one member forward in train mode on a random [4,3,128,128] batch and in eval mode confirm embed() output equals a reference slice-based computation (or simply that two eval calls are identical), and that export_onnx succeeds on CPU.
